slides.headline: October 30, 1909: a boy was born in Bombay who would found both India's top physics institute and its nuclear program.
Homi Jehangir Bhabha was born into a wealthy Parsi family in Bombay on October 30, 1909
slides.body: Educated at Cambridge, he started in mechanical engineering before pivoting to physics - a switch that would reshape India's entire scientific infrastructure decades later.

slides.headline: He founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research in 1945, then the Atomic Energy Commission of India.
slides.body: Widely credited as the principal architect of India's nuclear energy program, Bhabha died in the 1966 Air India Flight 101 crash near Mont Blanc - but the institutions he built outlasted him by decades.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat still runs on institutions one man's career pivot made possible.
slides.body: TIFR and India's nuclear program both trace back to a single engineering student who changed his mind about physics - proof that foundational infrastructure often starts as one person's redirected curiosity.
